findings.source: study finding listener-1 (details.html, "What the testers hit"; journal wf_13c0f539)
findings.title: Space replays an older answer because it plays the board in front, not the latest answer
where: skills/talk/static/call.js:1215 boardStart() returns the front board's answer when the voice is not on it
skills/talk/static/call.js:1232 togglePlay() tries boardStart() before play/pause of the current answer
skills/talk/static/call.js:1280 mediaKey(' ') routes Space to togglePlay
skills/talk/static/call.js:439 shownAnswer() falls back to lastAnswer() only when nothing is current
findings.evidence: After answer 2 (text-only, no board) arrived and the persona pressed Back 10 s, then Space, the panel started answer 1 from 0:05 of 0:20, the older Falling in answer, with the stage still on the Falling in board. The persona could not tell which answer Space would act on. The Space tooltip says only 'Play · Space'.
findings.cause: Play follows the board in front of the stage, which a text-only answer 2 leaves on answer 1's board. Space therefore plays that board's explanation from its cue. This is the 'Play of a board the voice is not on' rule. Nothing in the panel says which answer will play, and the conversation row of the answer about to play is not marked until it starts.
findings.reproduced: code reading of boardStart/togglePlay against shot 10 (Pause shown, answer 1 at 0:05/0:20, Falling in board in front); not re-run

skeptics.correction: The mismatch is stronger than the finding says. In the path I read, Back 10 s moved answer 2's audio, because answer 2 was `current`. Space then played answer 1, because `boardStart()` ignores `current` when the voice is not on the front board. So two adjacent controls act on two different answers. Cite `boardStart` and `togglePlay`, in `call.js` around lines 1215-1236. `shownAnswer()` is not involved in this path: it only matters for the `mediaKey` guard. The cause is the intended board-first rule, not a bug. Scope it as a missing cue (tooltip, or a mark on the row that will play) rather than a wrong action. "Major" is probably too high. Medium is more likely.

Describe it as intended behaviour with a discoverability gap, not a defect in the play logic. The gap is that nothing says which answer Play will start. The finding also says the persona pressed Back 10 s before Space. skip() only moves audio.currentTime and does not change which answer Space acts on. The cause is the board in front, and Back 10 s is incidental. Severity "major" looks high for a rule that is documented and deliberate. Minor to moderate fits better.

Three corrections. (1) The cause is not that answer 2 failed to become current: answer 2 is current and loaded at 0:00. boardStart() overrides it because frontBoard still points at answer 1's board, and a text-only answer does not move frontBoard. Line 439 (shownAnswer/lastAnswer) is not involved. (2) The rule is intended (comment above boardStart at call.js ~1211, and CLAUDE.md "Only a play of the board in front..."), so the defect is a mismatch in the page's feedback. The stage shows the reader with the answer-2 row marked and answer 2 loaded in the player, yet Play starts the older answer. A fix would let boardStart() yield when the answer in the player is newer than the board's answer and is not at its end. Failing that, the Space tooltip or the row marking would need to name the answer that will play. (3) Severity is more like moderate than major. The effect is a wrong answer replayed, which one press of the answer-2 Play button or Pause undoes. It only happens after a text-only answer follows a board answer. The cited lines are about right (boardStart ~1215, togglePlay ~1232).

With following on and the card's answer text-only the label is 'Play' or 'Play again'. Change the sentence in CLAUDE.md and references/call-page.md that says a play of the board in front redirects. where: skills/talk/talk.py:3451 call.add('status', status[:120]) stores a status as a permanent transcript entry
skills/talk/static/call.js:341 who==='status' renders it as a plain 'line status' with no state

findings.evidence: Progress lines the responder posts remain in the conversation as grey bullets long after the answer landed, so the transcript looks as if Claude is still working. Shot 05 shows 'thinking it through' above the finished answer 1, and shot 13 shows three of them among settled answers.

skeptics.correction: The cited line numbers are accurate (3451, 341/342, 2147). Line 2147 is only the export label, so it is weak evidence of the page's behaviour. Severity "minor" is fair. The effect is a history of progress notes that stay visible, not a wrong state. Whether the leftover lines are really misleading is a judgement. The grey bullets do not animate and no spinner is attached to them.

Shot 13's last line, "checking numbers", is the status of a turn still pending. It is the current line, so only the earlier ones are stale. The code line numbers are approximate: I confirmed talk.py around 3451 and call.js 342-343, but did not check the 2147 export label. The page does clear the live status once an answer lands: the foot's `#status` element is driven by `statusText()`. Only the copies left in the conversation list persist.

Keep it as minor or lower. The claim that the transcript "looks as if Claude is still working" is overstated. These are small, faint, non-animated lines, and the foot status line and the pill show whether Claude is actually working. The accurate framing is clutter: accumulated progress lines sit between settled answers. They are not a false "still working" signal. The line 2147 citation is the export label ("Claude, working"), which is not the page, so it is weak evidence. Whether a progress log should persist may be intended behaviour, since the entry is deliberately stored as a transcript entry, but nothing I read states that intent. The fix would be cosmetic (collapse or remove statuses once an answer for that turn lands, or add a past-tense style). It is not a trust failure.

where: skills/talk/static/call.css:214 .ib[data-tip]:hover::after places the tooltip 8px above the button over the conversation

In shot 13 the 'Back 10 s' tooltip stays open above the player and hides the start of the 'Claude is working...' line, which reads 's working...'. The tooltip stays because the Back button holds focus or hover after the click.

skeptics.correction: Drop the "conversation list's bottom alignment" cause. I could not find it in `.convo` or its children, so the source of the blank band is unexplained and needs a DOM check. The "thinking it through" line mid-pane after an answer has arrived may be a stale status row, which would be its own bug. Keep the tooltip cause (call.css:214). The "no blur" remark at call.js:1236 is only a mitigation idea, because the tip is driven by :hover and not by focus. The `.line.status` row sits in the conversation, above the player's own status text, so the tip collides with that text. Severity is minor.

The tooltip is driven by hover only, not by focus, so a missing blur is not the cause. It appears only with a hover-capable pointer, so touch devices do not show it. The "thinking it through" line in the gap shots is a marker inside the conversation list, not the "working..." status line above the player. The back handler is the `$("back").onclick` line, not a separate `skip(-10)` call. It is minor and transient, and clears when the pointer moves away.

Two parts of the cause are wrong or unproven. (1) The tooltip is hover-only. The rule is `:hover::after`, so the tooltip would not stay open from focus alone. Calling blur() in the click handler would not fix it, because the pointer is still over the button. A fix would be to place the tooltip elsewhere or hide it once the button is clicked. (2) The blank-gap cause is not shown. Shot 05 shows empty space both above and below the "thinking it through" line, which sits in the middle of the pane, not directly above the answer. So bottom alignment of a short list does not explain it. The line appears to be a status row rendered in place at the time of the turn, with the answer row and chips pushed down to the bottom. The gap above the first message is a minor oddity. The tooltip overlap is the real issue, and it is minor and desktop-pointer only.

findings.source: study finding listener-4 (details.html, "What the testers hit"; journal wf_13c0f539)
findings.title: No large, glanceable or audible state: thinking, speaking, ready and done look alike from across the room
where: skills/talk/static/call.js:543 appState() has four states (listening, working, speaking, idle) that only restyle small chrome
skills/talk/static/call.js:1291 the keydown handler gives Space and the arrow keys with no visible legend
skills/talk/static/call.js:1236 Back 10 s is the only seek control in the panel
skills/talk/static/call.js:823 autoplay is the only way a new answer announces itself
findings.evidence: The hands-busy listener could not tell without looking whether Claude was thinking, speaking or finished. Answers took 10 to 30 s and were missed. There is no cue when an answer is ready. The state is only the small pause or play icon, a grey bullet and a small status line. She also found no hint that Space works, no repeat-last-sentence control, and no queue.
findings.cause: The panel is designed for a reader at the screen. It has no sound cue on a new answer or on ready, no on-page keyboard hint (Space and the arrows appear only in the Play tooltip), and the play/pause icon is the speaking-state signal. With sound off in the harness, the 'no sound' part of this is not testable, but the missing visual state and missing shortcut hints are real.
findings.reproduced: code reading; the audible side is not testable with the silent stand-in voice

skeptics.correction: Three claims are overstated. (1) appState() (call.js:534) does not only restyle small chrome. It sets data-state on .app, and call.css:34-42 colours and animates an orbiting ring on the whole panel frame, with distinct colours for speaking, listening and working. Idle in Live mode gets a green ring. This is a real glanceable cue, though it is panel-sized and not a room-scale one. The state names are listening, working, speaking and idle, so "done" and "ready" are not separate states. They are both idle. (2) "Back 10 s is the only seek control" is wrong. The keyboard handler at call.js:1256 moves by a sentence with the arrow keys, so a repeat-last-sentence exists. It is undiscoverable except by the tooltip, so the real defect is the missing hint. (3) There is a sound cue in Live mode for the user's own turn (chime 520/700/880). The gap is only that there is none for an answer arriving. The line citations are slightly off: the keydown handler is near 1256, not 1291, and Back is at 1239. Severity "major" is plausible only for the hands-busy or TV use case.

The claim "only the small pause or play icon, a grey bullet and a small status line" is overstated. appState() (call.js:535-539) sets data-state on .app, and call.css:34-42 uses it to draw a colored animated ring around the whole frame: red when listening, accent and fast when working, Claude color when speaking, green when idle in Live mode. This is a large, glanceable state cue. There is also an always-visible mode chip (call.js:~600, "Press to talk" or "Live · listening") and a TV screen mode (data-tv). The ring is turned off for reduced motion (call.css:293). The call.js:1291 keydown line number may be stale. The Space handler is at about call.js:1256. "No queue" is wrong. A new answer that arrives while another plays is queued and announced in the foot (CLAUDE.md, `queued` in call.js). Autoplay does announce a new answer by starting to speak, so the missing "ready" cue only matters when autoplay is off or the sound is low. Real gaps remain: no sound or on-screen cue for "answer ready" outside Live mode, no visible legend for Space and the arrows, and no repeat-last-sentence control. Downgrade severity from major to minor or moderate, and narrow the claim to "the state ring exists but ready and done are not distinct from idle, and nothing is audible outside Live mode".

Narrow the finding to two points. There is no on-page hint for Space and the arrow keys, since the tooltip is the only place they appear. Outside live mode there is no audible ready cue, although autoplay of the answer partly serves as one. Drop the claims that state is not glanceable, that no repeat-sentence control exists (left arrow does it), and that there is no queue (`queued` plus the foot announcement). Severity should be minor, not major.

skeptics.correction: Minor corrections. (1) The line numbers are slightly off: the skip() definition is at 1212, the back button handler is at 1236 and jump() is at 1264, not 1219. (2) Sentence stepping is not only on the arrow keys. A spoken "back" command also uses jump(-1) (call.js:1711). Severity stays minor. The "sentence stepping is only on the arrow keys" part is by design (the comment at call.js:1256 says so) and only lacks a visible hint. skeptics.correction: Two corrections. First, the cited code lines are right, but the finding should say the status entry is only added while its turn is still open (accept_reply(final=False)). Two parts are overstated. First, the "large blank area around it" is not caused by the status line. Second, the "gap" between the status and the answer in shot 30 comes from that layout, not from the status entry. The accurate claim is that finished status lines stay in the transcript as faint one-line entries and are not folded or removed once the answer lands. Keep the severity minor.

Two corrections. First, the persistence is deliberate: status is a conversation entry kept as a history of what the session said it was doing. where: skills/talk/static/call-wait.js:298-310 sendAgain

findings.evidence: Send again posts the joined text of all in-flight questions as one new entry with replaces set. Afterwards the card restarts at Sent with the clock counted from the new entry, then goes back to Not picked up (the slow doorbell is a harness effect). The only confirmation is the 7 s line 'Sent again.'; no resend count, no time of the last attempt, no 'two questions as one'.
findings.cause: Merging is deliberate (Call.replace sets aside everything in flight; nothing is lost). The defect is missing feedback: the card keeps no memory of the earlier attempt and restarts its clock.
findings.fix: A persistent card line such as 'Sent again 1:12 ago, 2 questions as one'; keep the original sent time (or show the wait since the first send). Do not resend each question as its own entry (conflicts with the server's single replacement model).

skeptics.correction: The merge is by design and no words are lost; the gap is feedback.
'Not picked up' again afterwards comes from the harness doorbell, not sendAgain.
Narrow the fix to a persistent line and keep the original time; drop the per-question resend.

findings.source: round 2 trial persona greek
findings.title: The stage's own words are never translated: toolbar, board counter, step control, Copy, Key points and the empty stage
where: skills/stage/static/stage.js:110 (Back to the voice), :113 and :1926 (empty stage), :234 and :1669 (All shown / Next step), :256-258 (Copy, Copied, Copy failed), :465 area (Answer n / Earlier on Key points), :1245 (Board i of n), :1790 (Answer in the text field, or press Talk.)
skills/talk/static/call-stage.js:34-63 (the messages sent to the stage hold only theme and follow, no language)
skills/talk/static/call-i18n.js:495 (uiLang exists only in the call page)
findings.evidence: After the panel turned Greek the stage still said Board 2 of 2, Step 5 of 5, Copy, All shown, Back to the voice, the Key points board with ANSWER 1 in capitals (a CSS uppercase) and, before any board, 'The stage is empty' with Code/Diagram/Table/Page. Her Greek boards sat under an English toolbar; she rated the trial 7 of 10. Only the board's own content is marked lang el (langOf and GREEK, stage.js:133-136, 1130), and the stage frame's title is already translated by call-stage.js:118.
findings.cause: The r1 i18n (tr() in call-i18n.js) covers only the panel. The stage is a separate frame with its strings in stage.js, and the call page never sends it the language, so it cannot follow uiLang. Half-done S-greek-2.
findings.fix: Add a stage:lang message that call-stage.js sends on load and on each uiLang change (read uiLang as a global; do not edit call-i18n.js), and a small English/Greek word table in the stage used by every string listed (re-check the line numbers: stage.js:465's Answer n / Earlier and the Key points cap and Copy strings were not found at the cited lines); set lang on the toolbar; the Key points board's cap line and name come from the same table. A stage opened alone falls back to navigator.language. A test that every user-visible stage string has a Greek entry.

skeptics.correction: Cited line numbers are slightly off; the CSS uppercase explains ANSWER 1 in capitals. Severity 3 reasonable.
The stage frame's title is already translated, so only the stage's internal strings are English. Fix as proposed: stage:lang plus a small table.
Re-check the line numbers for 'Answer n / Earlier' and the Key points and Copy strings; the cause and fix stand.
